* Vendored flat assembler 1

Upstream: https://github.com/tgrysztar/fasm
Revision: 225ce90e81e69877ab42505f7713e3d3fd531d42

This is a source snapshot, not a git submodule. The upstream copyright and
LICENSE.TXT are retained verbatim; LICENSE/fasm.txt in the til root carries
the same license for distribution with til's dependency notices.

Local adaptation: SOURCE/ and all paths beneath it are lowercase because
upstream's assembly uses lowercase include names. File contents are unchanged.
The Linux x86-64 entry is source/linux/x64/fasm.asm.

Bootstrap with an existing FASM (tested with Ubuntu's 1.73.32):

#+begin_src sh
fasm vendor/fasm/source/linux/x64/fasm.asm vendor/fasm/fasm
chmod +x vendor/fasm/fasm
#+end_src

Run these commands from the til root. The resulting ignored executable is
the bootstrap seed for subsequent rebuilds. make's vendor phase and the FASM
build/run path compare it with the common and Linux x64 assembly/includes.
Stale sources are assembled to tmp/ and replace the old executable by rename
only after success. No binary download, manifest or cache is involved.

clean and clean_vendor retain this bootstrap seed. Linux x86-64 installation
ships an available assembler and LICENSE.TXT under lib/til/vendor/fasm/;
assembler sources are not installed. The runtime is installed separately at
lib/til/src/fasm/ext.fasm. An unbootstrapped compiler installation reports
that it is shipping runtime sources only; bootstrap and reinstall to add
the executable. Ordinary C builds remain independent of the optional tool.
